'''David Wolfe''' is a [[mathematician]] and amateur [[go (game)|Go]] player.

==Education and career==
Wolfe graduated from [[Cornell University]] in 1985, with a bachelor's degree in [[electrical engineering]].<ref name=li>{{citation|title=David Wolfe|url=https://ca.linkedin.com/in/wolfe-david|work=LinkedIn|access-date=2020-07-07}}</ref> He obtained a Ph.D. in [[computer science]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1994, with a dissertation ''Mathematics of Go: Chilling Corridors'' combining both subjects and supervised by [[Elwyn Berlekamp]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=97613}}</ref>

After working as a lecturer at the University of California, Berkeley from 1991 to 1996, as an associate professor at [[Gustavus Adolphus College]] from 1996 to 2008, and then as an adjunct faculty member at [[Dalhousie University]], he moved from academia to the software industry.<ref name=li/>  Wolfe was a fan of [[Martin Gardner]] and in 2009 he teamed up with [[Tom Malin Rodgers|Tom M. Rodgers]] to edit a Gardner tribute book.<ref>''Puzzlers' Tribute: A Feast for the Mind'' (AK Peters) {{ISBN | 9781568811215}}</ref>

==Books==
Wolfe is the author of books on [[combinatorial game theory]], including:
*''Mathematical Go: Chilling Gets the Last Point'' (with [[Elwyn Berlekamp]], [[A K Peters]], 1994; also published as ''Mathematical Go Endgames: Nightmares for the Professional Go Player'', Ishi Press, 1994)<ref>Reviews of ''Mathematical Go'':

*{{citation|last=Campbell|first=Paul J.|date=December 1994|doi=10.2307/2691006|issue=5|journal=Mathematics Magazine|jstor=2691006|pages=391–393|title=none|volume=67}}
*{{citation|first=Daniel Elliott|last=Loeb|title=none|journal=Mathematical Reviews|year=1995|mr=1274921}}
*{{citation|last1=Guy|first1=Richard K.|last2=Nowakowski|first2=Richard J.|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1995-00601-4|issue=4|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|mr=1568191|pages=437–441|series=New Series|title=none|volume=32|year=1995|doi-access=free}}
*{{citation|last=Hayes|first=Brian|date=July–August 1995|issue=4|journal=American Scientist|jstor=29775500|pages=381–382|title=none|volume=83}}
*{{citation|last1=You|first1=Zhiping|last2=Yorke|first2=James A.|date=September 1996|doi=10.1137/1038104|issue=3|journal=SIAM Review|jstor=2132518|pages=543–544|title=none|volume=38}}</ref>
